reviews.text: I've had the privilege of testing this game from quite early on in it's development journey, and it's only gotten bigger and better with time. The game has grown so much from where it started, and I'm excited to continue following along through Early Access. So, about the game: GladiEATers is a really fun game that allows you to cook up a variety of unique creatures to fight with in battles, while also doing a great job at story building to set the scene for a world with weaponised food, and introducing each of the chefs in their respective backstories. You can also play against your friends or a random opponent in online multiplayer. There's so many unique abilities for each creature and you can use these to build different teams that require a whole new strategy. I still haven't played with every possible combination and I've gone through a fair few fights! (I will guard my stats page with my life, nobody needs to see how many times I've been annihilated by my opponent because I didn't think ahead) The chef stories are a really nice touch that add another layer of depth to the game, you learn a lot about the chefs personalities and I find myself becoming quite invested in seeing them win. The battle system is really well thought out with buffs, debuffs, and unique effects. If you're a new player, I strongly suggest making use of the inspect system so you can read up on your opponents, I still get obliterated if I don't pay attention to what the enemy has planned for me! The amount of minigames to cook your GladiEATers gives the game a lot of replay value for me, there's still some that I haven't mastered, and a lot more to come before the game is fully released. It reminds me of playing Cooking Mama on my DS when I was a kid, and I feel like a kid again when I'm panicking as the timer ticks down while maniacally smashing up an avocado. There's also run customisation options to change things up and add an extra challenge. You can play in point-buy mode which skips the minigames and allows you to build a team with points that affect their grades. I've had fun with this mode, it's helped me try out new strategies through trial and error. (and saved me from crashing out a few times - it hurts a lot more when you lose the creature you've painstakingly cooked to perfection) If I have frightened you, fear not. You can very easily play the game and have a nice, fun, relaxing time. I have done that many times. I just can't write a review without having flashbacks to my failures. The game is not prohibitively difficult, I am just a fool. On to the details: I play a lot of indie games purely to enjoy the artistry behind them, whether it be through a unique concept, the art, or the music, so these are all a pretty big deal for me. This game has so much content that brings the world to life. The pixel art is so detailed, the chefs are diverse, and the GladiEATer designs are really unique - some of them are adorable, and others are... well, a bit monstrous. There's multiple animations for each creature that really brings them to life and makes the battle feel more exciting. There's really pretty art for all of the characters, and comics that add to the story building too. The battle music is so good. I've heard the chef themes a million times and I still get hyped and crank up the volume every time I'm up against Jemin. I really enjoy the music in the chef stories too, but I haven't gotten to hear it as much as I replay CALosseum mode the most. (I'd love to see a digital artbook and soundtrack release in the future!) All of the GladiEATers also have unique sound effects (my personal favourite is pancake call, it is so cute), and it's things like this that make the game feel impressively polished considering its the dev's debut release, and it's still in early access. There's obviously just been such care and attention to detail in the design of the game, and the entire team involved in bringing it to life are so talented. If you're a bit wary of getting a game in Early Access, I have a general idea of the roadmap and there's really exciting things to come. I've seen massive improvements to the game and so much extra content added since I first started testing. Everyone on the team seems to genuinely care about what they're creating here and I know they've invested so much into getting it to where it is today. There's a friendly community over on the MilkBubblesGames Discord if you're interested in joining in over there, the devs are really responsive and seem to genuinely appreciate any feedback or ideas. I'm excited to see how the game progresses through early access with a whole new audience enjoying the game and giving their feedback. TL;DR If you like supporting indie devs and artists, GladiEATers is a really fun game with great art, great music, and a lot of variety in how you can play. There's a surprising amount of strategy involved when it comes to figuring out how to make the most of the time you have during cooking minigames, and planning your team so their abilities work together well.

I typically don't leave too many reviews but I really think this game deserves some love. It has really unique "creature" designs and the cooking system adds a nice mechanical skill component to each run. Runs can be altered with "spices" and heat levels to mix up the game and the current roster of chefs allow for different play styles and team comps. I am looking forward to playing more! P.S. the pixel art here is stellar and some of the later food designs are so fun.

Great game!! Kept me entertained for so long and still so much more to do! Super looking forward to the rest of the chefs coming out and cooking all the other Gladieater creatures! I love cooking mama so I love that part of this game especially! The art is great - very intricate and lovely style! Music fits so well and the instruments sound cool!
真的很好玩！

制作组肯定是用心做了的，但是感觉不太适合我吧。我一开始是奔着烹饪游戏的目标来的，但是后来才发现完全不是这么一回事。黛安的故事线里操作流程太多了，但是整个上菜时间只有30秒，切出S等级的丁刚刚好用完，只够做到切丁或者切块，更别提开火烤食物了。时间太紧了，根本看不到后面的精灵长什么样就结束了。而且对手的精灵技能太拖沓了，烹饪学校里玛丽的战斗，巧克力杯子蛋糕和巧克力酱一直在用可可雾，拼命叠盾，把戚风蛋糕叠了90多层护盾，愣是变成了boss战。而且因为不知道会叠这么厚的盾，我只切了一个生番茄片作为攻击手。我切了两个洋葱丁一个番茄丁，根本打不动这么厚的血。磨蹭了好久才结束这个战斗。我又不是在竞技场，为啥非要打盾这么厚的敌人啊？
love cooking FLAMES EMOTICON

This game is deliciously fun. It’s got more flavour than a dry-aged ribeye, and enough challenge to make even the most stoic chef throw a pan across the room. "Finally, some good f***ing gameplay." — Not actually Gordon Ramsay, but he’d probably say it if he played this.
Controls are rough and plenty of bugs, but it just launched in early access. Outside of that, the cooking mini games to make your team are neat, really makes me think of fighting foodons.

The premise of the game is that you play a Cooking Mama style minigame to make the units which you will use in turn based combat. The better you do in the minigames, the better your units are. I really enjoyed this concept. I found the different food units so cute and creative and it was a blast to find broken synergies!
Interesting and fun gameplay! There are so many different combos and possibilities to explore. The story and art style are also mesmerizing. Cant wait to play more!

I have been play testing for GladiEATers since 2023, putting 30+ hours total into the earlier test builds and the demo pre-release. This game is truly something special. There is nothing quite like it. It has already solidified a place in my heart and top 10 games of all time. If you love monster taming, Cooking Mama and/or unique indie games this is a must play. These devs have truly put so much love, care and passion into this project and it shows.

Really really good idea. Surprisingly fleshed out with the story mode and colosseum mode. The writing is actually funny, which is rare. "The children yearn for the coops." Is a new fav of mine. The cooking gameplay is pretty much there despite being early access. There is a LOT of cooking creatures and mini games to do them. If you have any interest in monster tamer games even just for the combat I would recommend this game. My only nitpick at the moment is that the turns in combat take a while and the animations during the fights can be stiff or incomplete (despite the gorgeous idle animations). Not to critique the art though, this game is very pretty and stylized. Really looking forward to the games future.

[h1]想成为一名优秀的厨师，不仅要学会烹饪，还得会战斗！[/h1] [quote]关注小红瓶，回血在当下点击关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45932802/] 小红瓶游戏评鉴组[/url][/quote] [h2] 游戏背景介绍 [/h2] 《斗食战酱》是一款融合了回合制战斗与食材烹饪的游戏。 [h2]游戏故事简述[/h2] 几十年前，一群基因科学家发现了“CAL”粒子，它能使食物中的卡路里变得动态活泼，而因抢夺粒子，各国之间一度发生战乱，经过协商，各国最终同意使用“CAL”粒子转化成的美食精灵来争夺话语权…… [h2]游戏玩法[/h2] 游戏分为三种模式，斗瘦场锦标赛、厨师故事、多人游戏，开局只能选择锦标赛模式，厨师模式可以选择不同的厨师，亲身经历他们的故事与战斗。 进入游戏后可以用不同的食材制造各种形态的美食精灵，例如煮鸡蛋会变成蛋壳精灵。 想要将一颗好吃的鸡蛋变成水煮蛋精灵需要先经历一场小游戏，玩家要点击鸡蛋保持它的㓎没状态，想获得高分数需要精准点击到绿白环重叠时的那一刻。 最终获得的分数会转化为烹饪水平，不同的烹饪水平代表了精灵不同的数值，喵的，我还是有点小菜，才烹饪出来一个C级的蛋壳精灵。 蛋壳精灵可以进行剥壳，剥掉壳后它会变得更加强大，虽然变强的代价是裸奔，但是为了变强，对不起了，小鸡蛋（剥壳也要经历一场小游戏，但是这个很简单，轻松S级）！ 经历完这些流程后，就能选择上菜了，上菜顾名思义就是将美食精灵加入队伍之中，为我光荣的奉献生命战斗吧！ 而美食精灵上菜之后也能继续烹饪，例如鸡蛋可以做成生鸡蛋，生鸡蛋可以做成煎鸡蛋，你别说，这个蛋的用处还挺多，不仅能变身还能吃，牛而逼之。 完成这些流程后，就可以开始我们的第1场战斗了，那多的不说，少的不唠，煎鸡蛋我们就开造！不对，我们战斗开战，不是开造！ 光溜溜的剥壳鸡蛋和煎鸡蛋上场后，就到了游戏的战斗玩法，经典的回合制战斗，战斗中可查看技能属性与效果，上方的头像代表谁先出手。 我们的剥壳鸡蛋可以释放三个不同的技能，分别为蛋黄屁，蛋黄奔流与太极蛋壳拳，光听名字的话我还是比较喜欢蛋黄屁，而后使用蛋黄屁击败对手后，你也就正式成为了一名，大鸡蛋专家（同时也会解锁厨师故事与多人游戏模式）！ 游戏的菜谱还是很丰富的，一颗鸡蛋可以延伸出数10种不同的美食精灵，当然也不仅只有鸡蛋，还有番茄，茄子，洋葱等等多种食材。 [h2]游戏总结[/h2] 游戏融合了回合制战斗与烹饪小游戏玩法，感觉还是挺有意思的，每种食材都能延伸出大量的美食精灵，增加了许多的游戏性，烹饪小游戏简单易懂，就是看着看着导致我有点饿了。 每种食物都有挺多不一样的技能，并且每个厨师的故事也挺有意思的，战斗系统的话，我觉得只有特效我不太喜欢，其他方面还是挺不错的。 总的来说，如果你也喜欢这类玩法与画风，可以考虑入手体验体验。 欢迎加入:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/xiaohongping] 小红瓶游戏评鉴组[/url] 助您回血！

[h2] 是食神，也是……精灵大师！？ [/h2] 原以为《斗食战酱》是一款十分热血的烹饪游戏，没曾想游戏烹饪仅仅是参与战斗、强化进阶食物精灵的重要步骤而已，其故事背景讲述——因为科学家发现了CAL粒子，它会使食物中无生命的卡路里变得活泼，赋予食物生命力，因如此各国之间为了CAL粒子爆发战争，最后决定通过在CAL竞技场以美食精灵战斗来解决战争，而玩家将操控以不同食材为主的人物，亲手烹饪出属于自己的精灵，在斗瘦竞技场中赢下冠军！ 游戏主要以故事模式和斗瘦竞技场为主，故事模式来解锁游戏后续几位人物，只不过由于目前是抢先体验，仅有三位以不同食材为主的角色，玩家将在故事模式中了解她们的身世与参与竞技场的动机，其中不光仅有剧情，也有一些探索解谜玩法以及游戏中最核心的食物精灵战斗。 至于斗瘦竞技场则是游戏纯粹的战斗模式，在这个模式下玩家要不断参与比赛与更强的选手对抗竞争，最终夺得冠军，而玩家能通过赢得比赛来获取金钱，在局外解锁每个人物对应的更多食谱和各种能力。 而游戏的玩法流程也十分简单，但内容却十分有意思。要想要食物参与战斗，首先玩家要在规定时间内将一个普通的食材烹饪，每烹饪一道工序，都会使食物更加强大，例如第一个人物鸡蛋妹，她能将一颗鸡蛋打散或水煮，打散的鸡蛋能搅拌、煎、水煮，搅拌后的鸡蛋能炒蛋、煎蛋、蒸蛋；而直接的水煮蛋有着不同的蛋壳破损状态、脱壳后变成脱壳水煮蛋→溏心蛋→全熟蛋，这其中的每一道工序所呈现出来的鸡蛋各种状态都是数值不同、能力不同的食物精灵，而每个精灵的基础数值也要靠烹饪时游玩的各种烹饪小游戏来达成不同评分增加，但从体验上讲，各种状态下差异性都非常大，多道工序烹饪出来的食物或许数值很高，但实用性可能并不高，因为它们也会分为攻击、辅助几种职业分支。 战斗方面游戏就是回合制作战，最多6v6，通过食物精灵的速度决定先后顺序，并无太大区别，此外游戏有一个多人模式，能比拼厨艺的同时考验双方的作战能力。 [h2] 总结 [/h2] 总体来说，《斗食战酱》绝对是一款十分有趣十分新颖的以烹饪为题材的回合制战斗游戏，丰富的食物做法，都有着独属于它们的能力个性，不过游戏当前为抢先体验版，食物天马行空的种类不算太多，但也足够惊喜，后续也希望制作组在食物上做出更多创意，例如艾吉的鸡蛋和戴安的番茄洋葱能不能来个组合之类的，目前游戏汉化方面也不完善，不过正常体验没有问题。 [quote]漫话漫谈，期待关注:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44551694/]写生漫话家[/url] ←节约宝贵时间，阅读省流测评~ 欢迎加入漫话家的大家庭:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/14030826]写生漫话家[/url]←共同探讨游戏中的精彩片段，向玩家展现第九艺术的魅力~

[h1]食物也能用来战斗？ [/h1] 做菜的游戏见过，但是把食材加工成宠物的我倒是第一次见，而且这些食材的模样还有点克苏鲁的风格，想到这里就更掉SAN了。但是回到游戏的玩法上，将做菜和回合制战斗融合到一切确实有点东西，还带有一点图鉴属性，总是让人想看看还有哪些进化分支没有解锁。 [h2]故事背景 [/h2] 游戏分为故事模式和对战模式，故事模式让你了解角色的故事，熟悉一下角色的食材流派，第一个角色艾吉属于那种为了生计不得不参加比赛的角色，家里面负债累累，但有个生病的奶奶和三个妹妹要养，她的母亲为了生计不停的摆摊卖家里的蛋，但这些钱还比不上负债的增长。于是艾吉下定决心参加比赛，并在镇上的比赛获得了冠军，在拿钱回家的时候发现奶奶今天刚刚病逝。为了彻底解决家庭危机，她决定走向更高的厨师大赛。 [h2]游戏玩法[/h2] 玩法分为三个部分，一个部分游戏里的探索环节，可以推进故事进度；第二部分是战前的准备工作，也就是做菜环节。我们可以用不同的方式处理食材，比如鸡蛋可以蒸煮，也可以打散搅拌。这是两个不同的进化分支，煮鸡蛋剥皮后会获得一些防御力和强化buff；蛋液可以煎，往蛋卷的方向做，这样彻底放弃防御专心攻击；第三部分就是战斗环节了，类似回合制rpg游戏一样，根据双方的速度决定攻击顺序，玩家可以给敌人上debuff，推迟对面的攻击，也可以给队友上buff增加攻击力或防御力，从而更好的应对对面的阵容。 [h2]厨师手法很重要 [/h2] 处理食材的环节和做菜小游戏一样，有切菜切丁和前片不同的手法，切之前还要磨刀；鸡蛋的话煮鸡蛋、剥皮、搅拌蛋液、煎鸡蛋、鸡蛋切半然后加入新的制作手法，这些东西玩起来挺拟真的，有的还要控制温度和力度，要把握的比较精准才能获得S级的评分。另外这些所有的菜的准备时间是通用的，也就是说如果给你三分钟准备时间，你需要在有限的时间做好自己这边的全部上场阵容，还是蛮有难度的。 [h2]不足之处[/h2] 游戏玩法稍显拖沓，每次战斗前的做菜环节玩一次两次还行，要是每次都搞确实有点烦，但这和做菜游戏的本质很契合，每次做菜确实都是这样的，只能说两者都做到了精髓之处，但又因为各自的特点，拉长了游戏的战斗时间。另一点就是游戏还是抢先体验阶段，很多角色没出，流派也会少一些。 [h2]总结 [/h2] 《斗食战酱》是一款非常有趣的做菜类rpg游戏，题材新颖，玩法有趣，美术还有种怪诞风格，值得一试；不过做菜环节稍微有点麻烦，能接受游戏环节较为拖沓的玩家可以尝试一下这款游戏。 [quote] 游玩百态，将游玩心得用汉语化作玩家的指明灯，(๑•̀ㅂ•́)و✧ [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35402408/]点击这里关注汉化语录~[/url] 如果喜欢这个评测，请点个赞让更多人看见 [/quote]

Really fun game, played the demo a bunch already! Adding cooking-minigames and timepressure to the prep-stage is a great addition to the teambuilding-element of the tournament combat I am especially fond of the creature designs. A lot of the time CCs don't manage to have a continious design philosophy in regards to their creatures, but I am very happy that this is not the case here. The weird food-monsters are truly unique and I wish more games in the genre would move away from the overdone animal+element designs far too many of them use. Curious to see how this game develops over the course of EA!

I like this game a lot and the concept is super refreshing. But there are some MASSIVE bugs that are frustrating. It’s a fun game with lots of potential I do hope in the full game there characters who use more protein based foods such as burgers sushi ect because I feel more variety will really do the game good

GladiEATers is fun. That's it! The cooking games are fun, the stories are enticing, the creature combat is super compelling and every turn I have so much to consider ( but not too much!) I love love LOVE any game willing to put so much effort in crafting such beautiful pixel art, I can't believe how many animations there are! Coupled with a banging soundtrack and some truly heartfelt stories in the Chef Story mode, this game hit the nail in the head for me!!
I just nuked an army of onions with the power of Guacamole, this game is already worth the money in early access and I think it's only going to get better.

Fun little roguelite creature battler where you complete Cooking Mama style minigames to make your creatures, compounding bigger recipes for stronger versions of said creature (for example, turning a fried egg into an omelet, or dough into bread). It features various chefs to select from, each with their own cuisines and thus, different creatures and playstyles. There isn't a TON of creature variety (around 65 creatures at the time of this review), and there's slight overlap between chefs, but that's okay. I sort of wish we had more variation in cuisines, as right now it all seems to be heavily farm-fresh, vegan/vegetarian based dishes. Which is fine, but It would be cool to see more protein focused chefs, or just generally less healthy foods, like burgers, chicken, pasta, etc. I also do wish that some of the instructions for the minigames were clearer, as there were times I had to fail a few due to trial and error. I think this is mostly due to translation, as I noticed a few grammar errors in the dialogue as well. This is a deep-cut, but the artstyle and concept of this game very much reminded me of the classic Funorb flash game, Bachelor Fridge. It was my main inspiration for buying it and it did not disappoint! This game has a lot of potential for content growth, or even a sequel, and I hope to see it expanded upon! I even think this style would work wonders in a turn-based RPG, with the battling mechanics of Pokemon, but similar summoning mechanics to Fossil Fighters, where instead of excavating the creatures, you cultivate and cook them! Then you can combine them into stronger dishes! Anywho, fun game :)
